output.brief: The rise in write-offs is not a Haverlow problem. It comes from the night receiving cut. Haverlow's trailer data shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors opened, and the trailers were empty by about 23:00–23:40. The warm readings (6.6–7.9°C) were keyed at 02:31–03:18, hours after unloading. Since the night team went from six to four people, median time from dock to chamber has gone from 44 minutes to about 3h50. Product sits in unrefrigerated staging at roughly 15–17°C. Night write-offs rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day shift stayed flat. The chambers are holding temperature. Don't raise the chargeback or move volume. It would penalise a supplier whose product arrived cold, and it would leave the cause in place. Don't drop the night probe either, since it is the check that shows the problem. Restore the night team to six, set a maximum dock-to-chamber time, and track it weekly from scan data. Separately, request Corriebank's claim-level extract and check a sample of claims before changing their credit terms. Their credits rose after self-certification began, but part of that rise may be real spoilage from the warm dock. I'm fairly confident in the main diagnosis. The share of credits that are over-claims remains unknown.
